reason: Both meet all hard requirements (snapshot-first, no restart/failover before snapshot, correct section order), but Response B's abort/rollback conditions are more concrete and actionable (specific lag/disk thresholds, 5-minute reassessment windows, explicit restore-from-snapshot instructions), and its runbook adds practical rigor (IC/Scribe assignment, concrete commands like pg_stat_activity and VACUUM FULL, a time-to-full reassessment step) that make it slightly more usable as an actual incident procedure.
